source.title: Leveraging Guided Backpropagation to Select Convolutional Neural Networks for Plant Classification
source.authors: Sakib Mostafa; Debajyoti Mondal; Michael A. Beck; C. Bidinosti; Christopher J. Henry; I. Stavness

page_placements.theme: Data quantity and composition affect generalization

record.file_problem: none; full article text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study trains CNNs at different depths and reports training and test accuracy on natural plant datasets, bearing on how model capacity relates to generalization. It does not test the specific interventions or measurements in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports train, test, and validation accuracies in Table 1 and discusses how model depth and capacity relate to overfitting. The SSIM values are used to select model depth; they are not a measure of the train-test gap itself. Segmented-image accuracies in Table 2 concern background reliance, so they are left out.
record.test_reason: The study examines CNN depth, plant-classification accuracy, and similarity between guided-backpropagation visualizations. None of its experiments tests V1–V8. Depth comparisons do not test widening beyond interpolation, and visualization similarity does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness. Its discussion of Feldman and Zhang is cited background, not an example-removal experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that extracted features depend on capacity, early-layer visualizations are more diverse, and overfit models show a more distinct transition to similar deeper-layer visualizations. They propose SSIM cut curves as a potential aid for detecting overfitting and choosing depth early in training, while acknowledging that the elbow can be ambiguous.
record.recipe_differences: Plant classification on three plant datasets; random initialization, Adam, dataset-specific architectures, and guided-backpropagation/SSIM analysis; no random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model depth affect reported training and testing accuracy; the authors report different relative performance across Weedling, Plant Village, and Plant Seedling.

fits_no_version.finding: Depth changes have dataset-dependent performance: ResNet-50 reaches 96.70% testing accuracy on Weedling versus 95.14% for 3-Conv-ResNet, whereas Plant Village favors 3-Conv-ResNet at 99.29% versus 98.04% for ResNet-50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing convolutional depth does not uniformly improve held-out accuracy on these plant datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Reduced-data Weedling models reach 99.89% training accuracy but only 50.70% and 52.10% testing accuracy; their full-data counterparts reach 96.70% and 95.53% testing accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing training data can produce large generalization gaps in these CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report more diverse early-layer GBP visualizations, a sharper transition for overfit models, and similar SSIM curve patterns across training epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Similarity between layer visualizations may provide a heuristic for selecting CNN depth early in training.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The selected checkpoint is the one with the highest testing accuracy. The paper describes models as overfit based on accuracy differences, but does not report train-test error directly. Its conclusions are limited to the tested plant datasets and architectures.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports accuracy on segmented images for Weedling and Plant Village to assess background influence; omitted because it does not report the general train-test performance comparison targeted by these rows. Figures 4–12 report SSIM cut curves; precise values are not stated in the text, and the paper does not use SSIM as a direct measure of the train-test gap.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label training or matched natural-label versus random-label generalization comparison.
No width sweep, interpolation threshold, or test-error comparison beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No fully connected classifier comparison, local-connectivity intervention, or convolution-derived initialization.
Adam is used without an SGD comparison or optimizer-tuning experiment.
No batch-size comparison or evaluation of remedies for a large-batch penalty.
No dropout comparison or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, sharpness–gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures. SSIM compares feature visualizations.
No memorization-based example selection, removal and retraining, or matched random-removal control. Feldman and Zhang is cited only.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 1 accuracy values match the supplied text. The rows bundle three measures each. Their train–test gaps are calculable: for example, R2 is 49.19 percentage points. Failure to report error separately is not a measurement limitation because error equals 100% minus accuracy. The substantive limitation is that these measurements do not test V1–V8. Checkpoints were selected using maximum testing accuracy, so the testing set also served model selection. Table 2 and SSIM figures are already declared in rows_left_out and contain no missing tests of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test accuracy.
Varies model depth and architecture, not width in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks; does not test the interpolation threshold or double descent.
No fully connected image classifiers or comparison isolating local connectivity.
Uses Adam; does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or test optimizer tuning.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch test.
Measures SSIM between guided-backpropagation visualizations, not magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness or a comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized examples or compare retraining with random-example removal.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses memorization and generalization, including Feldman and Zhang (2020), without testing their memorization-based removal result.

tranche.reason: The study measures CNN depth, classification accuracy, and guided-backpropagation visualization similarity; none tests or uses the specific findings in V1–V8.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Section 2.5 selects checkpoints by maximum testing accuracy; the reduced-data models use 10% of training data, and their overfitting does not test any listed version.
